description: 64 human pass/fail judgements with free-text notes over 2 image models x 8 scenes x 4 takes
valid_v1_use: Historical failure-mode vocabulary; regression CANDIDATE list; evidence that face drift and text defects occurred in this project's own production attempts
invalid_use: Not current ground truth. Not a benchmark. Not a qualified instrument's output. Single unblinded rater, no protocol, no repeat.
notes: Recovered tonight from git history because spike/.gitignore whitelisted out/scores.json against an out/* exclusion. Reconciles exactly with canon/findings/FINDINGS-11: 64 items, 10 failures, nano 7/32, seedream 3/32.

description: 129 per-call cost ledger lines across 11 model/step labels, total $35.28
valid_v1_use: Historical cost-per-attempt reference; proof that a per-call cost ledger next to outputs is workable
invalid_use: Not a current price list. Prices are July-2026 fal.ai list values hardcoded in the script, not billed amounts, and the file's own comment says the ledger over-counts failed round-1 video attempts.
notes: The single most useful legacy artifact for Cost per Accepted Outcome: it is a real prior example of cost recorded per attempt rather than per session.

description: The 64 scored generated images themselves (nano_*.png, seedream_*.png)
valid_v1_use: Their scores and filenames are usable as a historical record and as a re-generation specification
invalid_use: Cannot be re-scored, re-annotated for multiple defects, or used as regression stimuli until the bytes are made accessible
notes: spike/.gitignore excludes out/* and whitelists only .gitkeep, costs.jsonl and scores.json. The images were never committed. Searched: all branches and all reachable commits of media-factory. Not present.

description: Video outputs of the film/lipsync/scene experiments (veo3.1, wan-25, seedance, sadtalker, latentsync)
valid_v1_use: Cost lines and script parameters survive and describe what was made
invalid_use: No media available for temporal or lip-sync regression use
notes: Same gitignore exclusion. 62 of the 129 cost lines are video/lip-sync steps, so the attempts are evidenced even though the outputs are not.

description: 3 first-party brand mark assets: aight_logo.png (680x240), logo_0.png (204x33), logo_1.png (237x74)
valid_v1_use: Candidate first-party logo/wordmark references for REQ-CAP-09 logo_wordmark_fidelity. Project-owned demo brand, so no third-party trademark exposure.
invalid_use: Not a substitute for the >=12 marks the product pack needs. Low resolution: two are under 240px wide, which limits fidelity testing.
notes: Genuinely useful find: 3 of >=12 marks, from a source the project owns. Visual inspection confirms aight_logo.png is the project's own 'Aight' wordmark. Resolution is the limiting factor, not rights.

description: 19 illustrated narrative storyboard frames used as image-to-video start frames
valid_v1_use: Historical record of an image-to-video experiment's inputs
invalid_use: NOT a person-reference pack. Visual inspection confirms these are AI-generated illustrated scenes, not photographs of identifiable people, so they cannot serve REQ-CAP-11 person_identity.
notes: Important negative result: these were the most plausible candidate for a legacy person pack and they are not one. Their own generation provenance (which model produced them) is not recorded anywhere in the repository.
Explicitly excluded by spike/.gitignore line 7. Never committed. Concrete search performed across all branches and reachable commits.

notes: Excluded by spike/.gitignore. Same class of reproducibility hole as the EVAL-005 pinned font: a build that depends on an uncommitted font asset cannot be reconstructed from GitHub alone.

description: 14 model-output samples: 12 video frames (6 wan + 6 comp) plus 2 headline stills (nano, seedream)
valid_v1_use: Historical checker-calibration stimuli; the material behind FINDINGS-01
invalid_use: Not a population. FINDINGS-01 itself records only 4 independent sources behind the 14 samples: the 12 frames are highly correlated, being frames of 2 clips.
notes: Already committed to this repository and verified present tonight. The correlation caveat is exactly the 'frames of one clip are one trial' rule that REQ-CAP-20 restates.
